answer: Sequential-work aging: a new agent binds its key to a verifiable delay function chain and posts a checkpoint hourly. Verifiers check each one cheaply, and voting weight grows with unbroken chain length, which parallel hardware cannot speed up. Any delta between claimed and verified age zeroes the weight. A public atlas of checkpoints makes audits easy. Each fake needs its own core, about ten dollars monthly, and a fresh dune of new keys carries almost no weight.
